title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck asks how to recover algebraically the analytic uniformization data of the fibres in a family of curves over a curve X. The ingredients are a P^1-bundle P_X, a section, a connection, and the developing map from the disc bundle tilde-X ⊂ P_X^an. This page gives the purely algebraic answer for a smooth curve X/S in characteristic 0, keeping only 'condition 1°' (transversality) and setting aside 'condition 2°' (the global, uniformization-type condition).

The structures of type a) b) c) are:
(a) a Severi–Brauer scheme P → X of relative dimension 1, i.e. a P^1-bundle / PGL_2-torsor;
(b) a section σ: X → P;
(c) a connection c on P relative to X/S.
Condition 1° is the transversality condition: σ is nowhere horizontal, so the Kodaira–Spencer-type map T_X → N_σ is an isomorphism. In modern terms these are Gunning's indigenous bundles, i.e. PGL_2-opers, i.e. projective structures.

Claims on the page:
(1) The category of such structures is rigid (no nontrivial automorphisms).
(2) Canonically P ≅ P(E), where E = J/J^3 ⊗ ω^{-1}. Here J ⊂ P^∞_{X/S} is the augmentation ideal of the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, and J/J^2 = ω, J^2/J^3 = ω^{⊗2}. So E is an extension 0 → ω → E → O_X → 0, with no theta-characteristic needed. This is the non-split (Gunning/Atiyah) extension. Its projectivization is the canonical PGL_2-bundle of opers, and σ is given by the line ω ⊂ E (or the quotient).
(3) The connection is encoded as an isomorphism P^∞_{X/S} ≅ O_{\hat P}. Here \hat P is the formal completion of P along σ, and the isomorphism is required to extend the canonical isomorphism to order 2 that comes from the construction of E. One transports the tautological connection of X×_S X → X (the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal) to \hat P, and requires that it come from a connection on P.

The next page concludes that such structures correspond bijectively to the lifts of the order-2 isomorphism to order 3, with no further condition. These form a torsor under Hom(ω, ω^{⊗3}) = ω^{⊗2}: the torsor of projective connections, with the Schwarzian ambiguity by quadratic differentials. The next page also identifies the adjoint bundle as Sym^2E ⊗ ω^{-1}, filtered with graded pieces ω, O, ω^{-1}.

Purpose: an algebraic theory of uniformization data (projective structures) in families, as input to Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs considerations.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. One point is left implicit: J/J^3 needs a choice of one of the two O_X-module structures on P^∞_{X/S}. Either choice gives an isomorphic extension class up to sign.

The sentence that reads 'On ne prouve pas les isom. tels que ...' is garbled. From the next page's conclusion (bijection with order-3 lifts) it is likely 'On trouve/prouve que les isom. tels que ... sont en correspondance...', not a negative statement.

ideas.what: P^1-bundle with section and connection satisfying transversality, forming a rigid category; called 'connexions projectives'
Canonical oper bundle E = J/J^3 ⊗ ω^{-1}, an extension of O by ω built from second-order principal parts, avoiding a choice of theta-characteristic
ideas.modern_name: jet-bundle description of the oper/Gunning bundle; adjoint bundle ≅ J^2(T_X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Gunning, Beilinson–Drinfeld, Frenkel–Ben-Zvi use J^1(ω^{-1/2}) or J^2(T))

ideas.what: Projective connection = identification of the formal neighbourhood of σ in P with the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, extending a canonical order-2 identification; the choices are order-3 lifts forming an ω^{⊗2}-torsor
ideas.modern_name: projective structures as third-order jets / Schwarzian; affine space of projective connections over H^0(ω^2)

missed.claim: A relative, characteristic-0 algebraic theory of projective connections / indigenous bundles over an arbitrary base S. It uses a theta-characteristic-free canonical bundle E = J/J^3⊗ω^{-1} and characterizes the connection via formal completion along σ ≅ formal neighbourhood of the diagonal. This anticipates the oper formalism of Beilinson–Drinfeld and Mochizuki's indigenous bundles over arbitrary bases.
missed.quote: les P (fibrés de S.D. de rang 1 sur X) sont canon. isomorphes à P(E) ... E ≃ J/J^3 ⊗ ω^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck had the oper picture (in rank 2) in the 1970s, in connection with uniformization and Gauss–Manin. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early, scheme-theoretic formulation of PGL_2-opers / indigenous bundles, with a neat theta-free construction via principal parts. The content is known (Gunning, later Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki), so this is a notable historical detail rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'connexion c_X sur P rel. à X/S' is probably 'connexion c sur P rel. à X/S'.
'de l'idéal 2 canonique' is likely 'à l'ordre 2 canonique' (the canonical order-2 isomorphism), consistent with 'relèvements ... à l'ordre 3' on the next page.
'{+P(σ)+}' is likely a superscript such as P^{(2)} indicating the order-2 truncation.
'On ne prouve[?] pas les isom.' is uncertain; it likely reads 'On trouve/prouve que les isom.'
'X ×_S X sur X': the tautological connection is on X×_S X over X via the first projection.
